newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes lower as NYMEX losses pressure.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes lower as NYMEX losses pressure.

text.p: IPE gas oil was dragged to a lower close on Tuesday as London tracked New York's erratic downward path, traders said.
May gas oil settled $1.50 off at $163.75 a tonne against an intraday high of $167.00 and low of $163.00.
June Brent, meanwhile, was trading 19 cents off at $18.15 a barrel at 1646 GMT against an earlier high of $18.64 and low of $18.03.
"It's been a disappointing day," said one trader. "We were expecting it at least to hold steady."
Traders said both gas oil and Brent had been pressured lower by losses on the May NYMEX crude contract which expires at the end of Tuesday's session.
"It's very choppy over there," said another trader. "And what the market does between now and expiry is anybody's bet."
Traders said the market was keeping close tabs on expected figures for American Petroleum Institute (API) U.S. oil stock data due out late on Tuesday after the IPE Brent market closes.

According to a Reuters survey, analysts estimated that crude stocks grew 1.0 million barrels, distillate stocks fell 500,000 barrels and gasoline stocks fell 1.3 million barrels in the week ended April 18.
In the week ended April 11, API data showed crude stock rose 2.973 million barrels, distillates 2.586 million barrels and gasoline 3.627 million barrels.
